text:
Frank Nazar has picked a good moment to take off. With Connor Bedard facing what reports call a potentially lengthy absence, the Blackhawks need someone to drive the middle of the ice, and Nazar has 9 goals in his last ten games, a six-game point streak and, as The Athletic's Mark Lazerus put it, a "42-goal pace." His ice time is up two minutes a night over that stretch, to about 19:23.

The speed is real: he sits in the 90th percentile for top skating speed and for shot speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries last season. The finishing is the part to hold loosely. He has 12 goals on 7.1 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 26% against 11% last season, and over the last ten games his chances have been his usual ones. Our numbers still project about 31 goals for the 22-year-old. What we'd watch is whether his shot quality climbs with the bigger role, because that is the part of a hot streak that sticks.
headline: Frank Nazar is carrying more of Chicago's load
